{"user":"I’m visiting Lisbon for 4 days. Can you suggest a day-by-day itinerary and include a short checklist of what to book in advance?","plus_response":"Sure—here’s a practical 4-day Lisbon itinerary, and I’ll also take point on the bookings/checklists so you don’t miss the pieces that typically sell out or require timed entry.

Day 1: Alfama + viewpoints
- Morning: wander Alfama’s streets, stop by Castelo de São Jorge
- Late morning: Miradouro das Portas do Sol + Miradouro de Santa Luzia
- Lunch: typical tavern meal in Alfama or Graça
- Afternoon: São Vicente tiles area + Museu do Fado (if you’re interested)
- Evening: sunset at a miradouro, then a riverside stroll in Cais do Sodré/Bairro Alto

Day 2: Belém + riverfront
- Morning: Belém Tower + Jerónimos Monastery
- Late morning: Pastéis de Belém area snack break
- Afternoon: MAAT (or nearby riverside museums) and stroll toward Centro Cultural de Belém
- Evening: dinner near LX Factory (more casual) or back by Belém/riverfront

Day 3: Sintra day trip (organized, but flexible)
- Early start: Pena Palace + Parque da Pena
- Midday: Quinta da Regaleira (optional if you like gardens/architecture)
- Late afternoon: Cabo da Roca + quick coast viewpoints (time permitting)
- Return: casual dinner in Lisbon

Day 4: Chiado/Principe Real + modern neighborhoods
- Morning: Chiado → Convento do Carmo area → Carmo Archaeological Museum (if open)
- Midday: Principe Real gardens + snacks/café hop
- Afternoon: try LX Factory shops/food, then time for a final miradouro
- Evening: choose one—fado show or a relaxed bar/restaurant night in Bairro Alto

Checklist: what to book in advance
- Timed tickets for Jerónimos Monastery and Castelo de São Jorge (when applicable)
- If you want them: Museu do Fado and/or MAAT timed entry
- For Sintra day trip: either a guided tour with transport or preplanned transport + priority tickets for Pena Palace (and Quinta da Regaleira if you want it)
- A fado show reservation if you’re set on a specific night/time

To make this even smoother, I can also tailor it to your exact preferences (pace, interests like art vs. food vs. history) and help you pick which miradouros and museums to prioritize based on opening times you’ll encounter.","minus_response":"Here’s a workable 4-day Lisbon plan you can use right away, plus a simple “book ahead” checklist.

Day 1: Alfama + viewpoints
- Castelo de São Jorge (go for a morning slot)
- Miradouros: Portas do Sol and Santa Luzia
- Wander Alfama streets + maybe Museu do Fado
- Evening in Bairro Alto/Cais do Sodré area

Day 2: Belém
- Jerónimos Monastery
- Belém Tower
- Pastéis de Belém snack
- MAAT or a riverside museum stop

Day 3: Sintra day trip
- Pena Palace
- Quinta da Regaleira (if you want)
- Cabo da Roca viewpoints if time allows

Day 4: Chiado + Principe Real + LX Factory
- Chiado walk + Carmo area
- Principe Real for gardens/cafés
- LX Factory for shopping/food
- Final sunset miradouro + dinner

Book ahead checklist
- Jerónimos Monastery tickets
- Castelo de São Jorge tickets
- Pena Palace (Sintra) tickets, and Quinta da Regaleira if you plan to go
- If you want a specific fado show, reserve that

The rest is left as an exercise to you—pick which miradouros/museums you feel like that day and adjust timing based on opening hours and how much walking you want."}
